content.title: About
content.content: Chocolate candy, peanut butter filled are small sweets coated with milk or dark chocolate and filled with a smooth peanut butter paste. They are popular as a quick snack and are commonly found in confectionery assortments.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first peanut‑butter‑filled candy recipe appeared in the United States in the early 1920s.
Peanut butter filling is usually made from roasted peanuts, sugar, and a small amount of vegetable oil.
Chocolate shells can contain up to 30 % cocoa butter, giving them a glossy snap.
These candies are often used in marketing as an “energy‑boosting” snack because of the sugar‑protein combo.

items.title: Source of protein
items.content: Peanut butter provides plant‑based protein that helps support muscle maintenance.

items.title: Contains healthy fats
items.content: Peanuts are rich in monounsaturated fats that are beneficial for heart health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Peanuts contain niacin, thiamine, and folate, which are important for metabolism.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Dark chocolate supplies flavonoids that may protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Quick energy snack
items.content: The combination of carbohydrates from chocolate and fats with protein from peanuts provides a rapid energy boost.

items.title: Peanut allergy
items.content: These candies can trigger severe allergic reactions in individuals sensitive to peanuts.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: The added sugar makes them calorie‑dense and may contribute to tooth decay if consumed frequently.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: A typical serving (≈30 g) can contain 150–180 kcal, so portion control is advisable.

items.title: Trans‑fat presence
items.content: Some manufacturers use partially hydrogenated oils in the chocolate coating; choose trans‑fat‑free versions when possible.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy the candies straight from the package, stir them into ice cream or yogurt, or use them as a sweet filling in baked goods.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the candies in an airtight container in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. For longer shelf life, store them in the refrigerator to prevent the chocolate shell from melting.
